items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: INTERVIEWER: He's supposed to be related to Toka somewhere. [INTERVIEWEE] That's right. That's the uncle of Toka.

ctx.x: Powers. His name was Ambrose Powers? Powers, yeah. I figured you'd know that. He's supposed to be related to Toka somewhere.

That's right. That's the uncle of Toka. That's Ambrose Powers. He played, uh, well, he, uh, he played, uh, guitar, violin, and trombone. Oh, sure. I didn't know that. Yeah, he played things pretty good. He played mandolin too. Did you ever work with him much? Oh, that's my first start with them men. Yeah, he's one of the men that carried me out. Yeah, he's one of the men that first carried me out between, uh, you can say, uh, him and, uh, T. Rochon, Gilles Duvarny. Well, those men, uh, carried me out.
